mcqs.question: What is the definition of inflorescence in flowering plants?

options.A: The arrangement of leaves on a stem
options.B: The arrangement of flowers on the floral axis
options.C: The type of fruit produced by a plant
options.D: The process of pollination in a flower

mcqs.answer: The arrangement of flowers on the floral axis
mcqs.explanation: Inflorescence refers to the pattern or arrangement in which multiple flowers are borne on the floral axis of a plant. Option B states this definition, whereas the other options describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes a racemose inflorescence?

options.A: The main axis terminates in a flower, stopping further growth
options.B: Flowers develop from the tip of the axis first (acropetal)
options.C: The main axis continues to grow and produces flowers laterally along its length
options.D: Each flower is borne on a separate stalk without any main axis

mcqs.answer: The main axis continues to grow and produces flowers laterally along its length
mcqs.explanation: In racemose (indeterminate) inflorescences the main axis keeps elongating, and flowers are produced on lateral pedicels, matching option C. Options A and B describe determinate or opposite patterns, and D ignores the central axis.

mcqs.question: Cymose inflorescence differs from racemose inflorescence in that:

options.A: The main axis terminates in a flower
options.B: The main axis keeps elongating indefinitely
options.C: Flowers are borne only at the base of the stem

mcqs.answer: The main axis terminates in a flower
mcqs.explanation: Cymose (determinate) inflorescences end their growth when the terminal flower forms, so the main axis stops, which is described in option A. In racemose types the axis continues to grow (option B). Options C and D are inaccurate descriptions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following plants exhibits a racemose type of inflorescence?

options.A: Lily, which bears a single flower
options.D: Rose, which shows a cymose arrangement

mcqs.explanation: Wheat bears a spike, a form of racemose inflorescence where sessile flowers are attached directly to an unbranched elongated axis. Lily (A) has a solitary flower, sunflower (B) has a capitulum (a type of head), and rose (D) typically shows cymose branching.

mcqs.question: In a plant where many small flowers are arranged along a common stem, as seen in lily of the valley, this arrangement is called:
mcqs.explanation: The cluster of multiple flowers on a single axis is the definition of an inflorescence. Leaf phyllotaxy (A) refers to leaf arrangement, fruit cluster (C) to mature fruits, and root system (D) is unrelated.

mcqs.question: A gardener notes that the main stem of a plant keeps elongating, with new flowers appearing at the tip while older flowers are positioned lower down. Which type of inflorescence is this?
mcqs.explanation: The described pattern—continuous growth of the main axis with younger flowers at the apex and older ones below—is characteristic of racemose (indeterminate) inflorescences. Cymose (A) terminates growth, umbel (C) has a different architecture, and spikelet (D) is a component of grasses.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about cymose inflorescence is incorrect?

options.A: The main axis ends in a flower
options.B: The youngest flowers are produced at the tip of the axis
options.D: Lateral branches may also terminate in a flower

mcqs.answer: The youngest flowers are produced at the tip of the axis
mcqs.explanation: In cymose inflorescences the youngest flowers are actually at the base because the terminal flower forms first, making option B a common misconception. Options A, C, and D correctly describe cymose characteristics.

mcqs.question: If a plant displays a flat‑topped cluster of many small flowers, each on a short stalk arising from a common point, which type of inflorescence does it represent?
mcqs.explanation: An umbel consists of several pedicels of nearly equal length that spread from a single point, forming a flat or rounded top—exactly as described. A spike (A) has sessile flowers, a raceme (B) has elongated axis with spaced flowers, and a cyme (D) is determinate with a different branching pattern.
